sentences.text: Court No. - 71 Case :- APPLICATION U/S 482 No. - 9579 of 2023 Applicant :- Smt. Bilkish And Another Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Mohammad Belal Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Heard Sri Mohammad Belal, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri B.B. Upadhyay, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants Smt. Bilkish, Shaukeen,
with the prayer to quash the entire proceeding of Complaint Case No. 340 of 2009, Smt. Sayera vs.
Farzana and others, under Section 420 I.P.C. as well as summoning order dated 12.5.2009 and bailable warrant dated 29.11.2018 and N.B.W. and proceeding under Section 82 Cr.P.C., dated 22.11.2022 and proceeding under Section 83 Cr.P.C. dated 2.1.2023 in the aforesaid case which is pending before the court of Additional Chief Judicial (Junior Division) IInd, Hapur, and with the further prayer to stay the further proceeding of said complaint case as well as summoning order,
Smt. Bilkish And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134295927/
1 bailable warrant, non bailable warrant and proceeding under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and proceeding under Section 83 Cr.P.C., during pendency of the present application.
At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicants states that he does not want to press the prayer for quashing of entire proceedings of the case, summoning order, bailable warrant, non bailable warrant and process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and process under Section 83 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Bilkish And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He states that the purpose of the applicants would be served if they are permitted to appear before the trial court within a period of three weeks from today and file a regular bail application but till then the non-bailable warrants as issued may be kept in abeyance.
Learned counsel for the State has no objection of aforesaid arguments of learned counsel for the applicants.

In view of the above, the prayer for quashing of entire proceedings of the case, summoning order,
bailable warrant, non bailable warrant and process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and process under Section 83 Cr.P.C. is dismissed as not pressed.

However, in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the limited prayer of learned counsel for the applicants, it is directed that if the accused-applicants appear and apply for bail before the court concerned within three weeks from today, the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.
Till the aforesaid period, the non-bailable warrants and the process under Sections 82/83 Cr.P.C. shall be kept in abeyance.
It it clarified that if the accused-applicants do not appear before the court concerned by the said date, the court concerned shall proceed against them in accordance with law.
The present application is disposed of.
